problems.title: Cross-model gains require a common population
problems.source_location: Kinetics-600 Tables 1–2; author README, lines 146–156; official pre-paper MoViNet evaluation configuration
claim: Author documentation explicitly identifies still-accessible labeled test videos, while the cited baseline configuration uses validation data. Baseline values match the official model table.
analysis: For author set \(S_G\), baseline set \(S_B\), the reported difference decomposes as \[A_G(S_G)-A_B(S_B)=[A_G(S_G)-A_B(S_G)]+[A_B(S_G)-A_B(S_B)].\] The second term is unmeasured. A baseline scoring \(72/100\) on one set and \(78/100\) on another can appear \(6\) points behind an identical-prediction modified model tested only on the latter. This establishes non-identification, not actual video-set difficulty. An unseen matched rerun could resolve it.
result: Matched manifests/predictions are required. The internal attention-only versus GRW ablation may remain informative if its protocol is shared; the strongest split evidence concerns MoViNet, not automatically every row or Kinetics-400.
repair: Evaluate all checkpoints on one frozen labeled manifest, with clip/crop and compute conventions explicit. The existing author subset clarification is credited but does not supply matched baseline results.
problems.existing_correction_status: The authors already published the test-subset clarification. A matched baseline evaluation resolving this comparison is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: A documented comparison limit does not itself measure the true matched gain or falsify individual scores.

problems.title: A relative span theorem does not imply unit norm
problems.source_location: Affine-normalization discussion; Appendix A, anchored scalar theorem and Propositions 1–2
claim: The main text attributes near-unit-sphere embeddings to affine-map/GRW optimization; the appendix proves a relative anchored bound.
analysis: Translation by \(c\) leaves all velocities, accelerations and permuted energies unchanged, so \(L_\alpha(Z+c)=L_\alpha(Z)\). Changing affine bias realizes arbitrarily large norms with identical regularizer. This does not refute the theorem’s anchor \(z_1=0\), or analyze classifier/weight-decay interactions. The anchored scalar span proof remains valid.
result: Relative scale does not establish unit radius or shell concentration; empirical norm claims need their own distribution and normalization convention.
repair: For any loss sublevel \(L_\alpha(Z)\le\log((T-1)!)\), nonnegative ordering loss and Cauchy–Schwarz give \[\|z_j-z_1\|\le\sqrt{2(T-1)\log((T-1)!)/\alpha}\]. This is relative and conditional, not a unit-sphere theorem.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The error overstates a valid idealized theorem; it does not invalidate smoothing or observed benefits.
